It's easy to make a laundry list of things you "could" do that will help, but if the list becomes lengthy it's also very easy for it to become overwhelming and send you spiraling into further despair because you couldn't even complete the list.

Don't make a list; instead, find one thing you need to fix. Even if there are other issues you know about, just focus on the one task until you know you've completed it.

For example, maybe it's your diet and cooking. Maybe you find it really easy to get fast food most nights because there is no cooking involved and you find it "cheap". Maybe you hate cooking, maybe you just don't like the time it takes to cook, or maybe you just don't think you're good at it. Spend some time making a few basic healthy meals each night and work your way up from there.

Another great place to start is regular doctor visits. It might take a few Dr's until you find one that you can talk openly with, but it's very important to be aware of your health and current issues so they don't get worse.

Exercising is another great way to improve energy and health. You'll want your diet in order before you try adding in regular exercise though; If you don't have the energy or motivation due to a poor diet, exercising regularly can be very difficult to do because your body simply fights you every time you try.

People often mention "finding a hobby" but I've found this is the toughest one to solve first - If you're depressed, you usually don't have the energy or motivation to try something new, so this becomes another mental block. Once you fix the energy and motivation problems, new hobbies will come naturally or with just a little effort.

tl;dr Take it slow and easy, focus on fixing one thing at a time.
If you're struggling with depression, loneliness, low energy, or a feeling of wanting to give up, don't try to change everything at once. Instead, focus on one thing at a time, like diet.

It can be very difficult to relax when you are under stress. I may be a slow learner, as it took me a couple years to learn and develop a method of relaxation, but I have a few books I recommend that can help start providing ideas. Two of them focus on mindfulness meditation. Please don't disregard mindfulness as anything hippy-like or some form of new-age bullshit. Mindfulness meditation has an immense body of scientific literature supporting its benefits, and if you are unable to locate these scientific sources, I can share them with you.

The first book I recommend is Sam Harris' "Waking Up" (Although if you are a Christian, you may not like his secular approach, but I still think it is extremely helpful).

The second book is Jon Kabat-Zinn's "Wherever you go, there you are" Some parts of this book werent relevant to me and my lifestyle, but there was much in the book that was. It will provide ideas of how you can incorporate mindfulness into your life.

The reason mindfulness is so important is because we are constantly bombarded with information all day long from various sources, and mindfulness is a means of being aware of the present moment. Because essentially all problems related to anxiety and depression are tied to thoughts of the future or of the past, being in the present moment temporarily removes those negative feelings, and allows your body to relax on its own.

The third book I recommend is Viktor Frankl's "Man's search for meaning" I think he may be a Jew, and that seems to be something many goats hate, but the message in the book is simply about how to not just survive, but how to thrive, when under serious forms of stress and oppression.

Another thought.

If you use anything like alcohol, marijuana, or nicotine to relax, then you will be fighting an uphill battle. It is easier to relax, in general, when you don't have something clouding your judgment.
